title: Budget-aware retry defaults and session idempotency model for cross-SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) default strategy that (1) prevents runaway retry cost under heavy token/call charge, (2) exposes ergonomic idempotency primitives that cover single RPCs, multi-part uploads, and long-lived streaming sessions, and (3) defines a small, deterministic retryable-error taxonomy used by SDKs and server-side guards. We want defaults that are safe for production apps out of the box, but pluggable when customers need to tune for latency or throughput.
background_and_motivation: Current SDK behavior varies across languages and client libraries: some SDKs retry aggressively on transient network errors, others have minimal backoff which leads to thundering replays. We also lack a consistent, documented mapping from server error codes to SDK retry decisions and a clear conversation about idempotency scope for streaming and multipart requests. This causes: (a) unexpected cost spikes for customers with high per-token billing, (b) duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent server endpoints, and (c) confusion in debugging when streams rehydrate vs. duplicate-generation occurs.
design_proposal_summary:
Introduce three coordinated pieces:
1) Budget-Aware Retry Profiles: default profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) encoded as small JSON presets. Each profile contains: initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_ratio, max_attempts, and per-call token-budget guard (max_tokens_retry, token_window_seconds). SDKs will decrement a per-request token budget when retrying to avoid unlimited cost.
2) Session Idempotency Model: define explicit idempotency scopes: request-scoped, upload-scoped (multipart with part ids), and session-scoped (long-lived streaming session identifiers). SDKs provide helpers: IdempotencyKey() generator, SessionToken() lifecycles, and helpers to attach part_id for chunked uploads.
3) Unified Retryable Error Taxonomy: a three-tier taxonomy (TransientNetwork, RateLimited, Permanent). Each server error code maps to a tier via HTTP status + subcode headers (e.g., x-rw-error-code). SDKs consult the taxonomy for deterministic retry decisions and emit telemetry events for every classified decision.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-SDK presets implemented and shipped in python/typescript/go official libs
Default profile (balanced) prevents >2x token cost from typical 503 spikes in internal load tests
Idempotency helper APIs available in each SDK with examples for request, multipart, and streaming flows
Server-side mapping headers documented and adoption plan shared with backends
Telemetry captures retry_decision, error_tier, token_cost_of_retries for >=95% of retry events
examples_and_snippets:
Python: from redwood_sdk import RetryProfile, idempotency_key
profile = RetryProfile.preset('balanced')
resp = client.generate(..., retry_profile=profile, idempotency_key=idempotency_key())

Go: // attach part_id for multipart
partID := rwid.GeneratePartID()
client.UploadPart(ctx, uploadID, partID, chunk, WithRetryProfile("conservative"))
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Token-budgeting at the SDK level adds complexity for library implementers and may be conservative for bulk low-cost calls. Alternative: require server to return remaining_quota per-request, but that is slower to adopt.
Session-scoped idempotency requires a short-lived server-side ledger for session IDs; alternative is client-only optimistic resume with risk of duplicate side-effects.
Keeping the taxonomy small reduces developer cognitive load but may hide nuanced retry policies for niche error codes. We prefer a small surface with the ability to opt into full-code maps.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize presets and public spec; API review with SDK maintainers
Week 2: Implement presets + idempotency helpers in python SDK; run integration tests with internal staging backends
Week 3: Implement TypeScript + Go shims; complete telemetry instrumentation
Week 4: Publish docs, announce migration guidance, and flip default in new minor release after 2-day canary
migration_notes: Existing customers: no immediate break. New default is conservative-balanced. Provide opt-out via retry_profile=null to preserve old behavior.
Servers: add optional header x-rw-error-code mapping to help clients classify — if absent, SDKs fallback to HTTP status heuristics.
Monitoring: add dashboard chart for "token_cost_of_retries" and a signal when retries increase token spend >20% over baseline
testing_plan: Unit tests for presets and budget accounting across languages
Integration tests simulating 500/503 spikes to validate cost containment
Chaos test: intermittent connection resets during streaming to validate session resume semantics
E2E with a backend feature-flag enabling x-rw-error-code to verify classification mapping
